title: Basis-independent coherence and quantum correlations in two dipole-dipole-coupled electrons in double quantum-dot molecules
authors: Zakaria Bouafia, Neha Pathania, Mostafa Mansour
abstract: This work examines the thermal dynamics of basis-independent quantum coherence and correlation-based quantum resources for two dipole-dipole-coupled electrons confined in spatially separated quantum-dot (QD) molecules. Single-dot quantum superpositions and inter-subsystem coherence are characterized by using localized and collective coherence. Quantum correlations between the two double quantum dots are quantified by employing Bures distance entanglement, Local quantum uncertainty (LQU), and local quantum Fisher Information (LQFI). The findings show that dipole-dipole coupling $K$ is the most effective protective parameter, extending the entanglement sudden death temperature, diminishing the local quantum superpositions and enhancing the collective coherence. The dipole-dipole interaction has also a crucial impact on protecting LQU and LQFI beyond the entanglement sudden death temperature. Coulomb repulsion $J$ reinforces this protection through an independent channel, projecting the thermal state onto the entangled $\{|0_A 1_B\rangle,|1_A 0_B\rangle\}$ subspace; their combined action is required to approach the entanglement maximum, and it enhances collective coherence and extends the temperature range over which LQU and LQFI remain appreciable. Energy detuning $\varepsilon$ can enhance localized coherence but paradoxically accelerates the entanglement sudden death and quenches LQU and LQFI by weakening two-body correlations. Inter-dot tunneling $Γ$ enhances local superpositions at low temperature, but it reduces collective coherence, lowers the entanglement sudden death temperature, and disrupts other nonclassical correlations.
summary: This paper analyzes the thermal stability of quantum coherence and entanglement in two coupled electron systems within double quantum dots. It demonstrates that dipole-dipole coupling is superior to other mechanisms for protecting these non-classical resources from temperature-induced decay. The findings guide the design of robust solid-state qubits by identifying optimal parameter regimes.
main_problem: The study investigates how basis-independent quantum coherence and various correlation-based quantum resources decay under thermalization in a coupled electron system.
main_result: Dipole-dipole coupling ($K$) is the most effective parameter for protecting these quantum resources against temperature increases, significantly extending the entanglement sudden death temperature. The combined action of $K$ and Coulomb repulsion ($J$) is crucial for maintaining high levels of coherence and correlation.
method: The authors analyze the thermal dynamics by calculating various quantum measures—including basis-independent coherence ($	ext{CL}, 	ext{CC}$), Bures distance entanglement, Local Quantum Uncertainty ($U$), and local quantum Fisher Information ($Q$)—as functions of temperature and coupling strengths.
model_or_system: The system models two spatially separated double quantum-dot (DQD) molecules containing single electrons. The interactions include inter-electronic Coulomb repulsion ($J$) and dipole-dipole coupling ($K$), alongside tunneling ($\Gamma$) and energy detuning ($\epsilon$).
key_observables: Basis-independent coherence ($	ext{CL}, 	ext{CC}$), Bures distance entanglement ($	ext{Bd}$), Local Quantum Uncertainty ($U$), and local quantum Fisher Information ($Q$).
important_parameters: Dipole-dipole coupling ($K$), Coulomb repulsion ($J$), Inter-dot tunneling ($\Gamma$), Energy detuning ($\epsilon$), and Temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed using the Gibbs state $ho(T) = \exp(-\hat{H}/k_BT)/Z$ for finite temperature studies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how quantum resources depend on parameters like $J$ and $K$, showing that increasing $K$ dominates the protection of correlations, while tunneling ($\Gamma$) generally degrades collective coherence.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the theoretical measures used (Sec. 2), details the physical model (Sec. 3), presents the results analyzing parameter dependence (Sec. 4), and concludes with implications for quantum resource management (Sec. 5).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed quantitative comparison of multiple metrics for quantifying non-classical correlations, offering specific guidelines on which physical interactions ($K$ vs $J$) are most robust against thermal decoherence in solid-state qubits.
